# Temple Scroll Column 21 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 21 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 21:1 — "squared" vs. "square" vs. "perfectly square"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "squared it shall be" | Preserves Hebrew adjectival form rabu'a with literal syntax |
| LOGOS | "it shall be square" | Standard English phrasing for the geometric description |
| PNEUMA | "perfectly square" | Adds "perfectly" for emphasis and clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "it shall be square." Natural English phrasing without PNEUMA's interpretive addition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:3 — "pots" vs. "ash-buckets" / "flesh-hooks" vs. "meat-forks"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "pots... flesh-hooks" | Traditional biblical English for siyrotayv and mizlegotayv |
| LOGOS | "pots for the removal of ashes... flesh-hooks" | Adds clarifying gloss to "pots" |
| PNEUMA | "ash-buckets... meat-forks" | Modern functional equivalents for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS wording: "pots for the removal of ashes... flesh-hooks." Temple implements retain traditional names with clarifying context.

**Status:** Resolved with LOGOS wording.

---

## 21:8 — "showed" vs. "revealed"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "as I showed you on the mountain" | Direct translation of har'etikha |
| LOGOS | "as I revealed to you on the mountain" | "Revealed" captures theological weight of divine disclosure |
| PNEUMA | "as I showed you on the mountain" | Simple, clear rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/PNEUMA: "showed." The Hebrew har'ah means "to cause to see"; "revealed" imports theological overtones not inherent in the verb.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/PNEUMA.

---

## 21:10 — "most holy" vs. "supremely sacred"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "most holy" | Standard rendering of qodesh qodashim |
| LOGOS | "most holy" | Traditional and precise |
| PNEUMA | "supremely sacred" | Fresh phrasing to convey the superlative force |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS: "most holy." Universally recognized rendering of qodesh qodashim.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 21:11 — "nakedness be not uncovered" vs. "nakedness be exposed" vs. "body is exposed"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "your nakedness be not uncovered upon it" | Literal rendering preserving Hebrew idiom |
| LOGOS | "lest your nakedness be exposed upon it" | Formal English with "lest" construction |
| PNEUMA | "so that no one's body is exposed upon it" | Shifts from "nakedness" to "body" for modern sensibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "lest your nakedness be exposed." Retains the specific concept of 'ervah while using natural English syntax.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:15 — "stranger" vs. "unauthorized person" vs. "outsider"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "stranger" | Direct translation of zar |
| LOGOS | "unauthorized person" | Clarifies priestly authorization restriction |
| PNEUMA | "outsider" | Modern equivalent conveying exclusion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "stranger" (EMET) with LOGOS's clarifying phrase about lineage. The term zar is well-known biblical vocabulary.

**Status:** Resolved with composite phrasing.

---
